rationale:
The requirement has two obligations: `dependencies()` returns a snapshot of the observations collected so far, and later reads keep contributing to the same execution.

`crates/trust-but-verify/src/graph/validation_tests.rs#fn[snapshots_record_exact_reads_and_retain_distinct_versions]` covers both.
- **Empty start:** on a fresh context, `dependencies()` is empty.
- **Snapshot after a read:** after a read of node 1 returns "before", `earlier = inspection.dependencies()` equals `[Dependency::Node(1, fp("before"))]`.
- **Snapshot is detached:** the content is then changed to "after" and read again. `earlier` is asserted equal to the one-element vector only after those later reads, so a snapshot that aliased live state would fail.
- **Later reads contribute:** a fresh `dependencies()` call returns `[Node(1, before), Node(1, after)]`. Both versions appear, in order, and the repeated reads of "before" are not duplicated.
- **Collection continues after a call:** `finish` produces a record whose dependencies equal the same two entries. So calling `dependencies()` did not consume or reset the collected state.
- **Failed read:** a read of the missing node 2 fails and adds no dependency.

The public API test `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/public_api.rs#fn[public_exports_match_the_appendix]` only checks the exported signature inventory. It adds nothing behavioral and needs nothing more.

Only node reads are recorded as observations. A search of `crates/trust-but-verify/src` found only `record_read`, which records a node and fingerprint, and found no recording of edge observations in the context. I therefore did not treat the edge-label type parameter as a separate obligation. I found no unacknowledged gap.

text: Return a snapshot of the observations collected so far. Later reads continue to contribute to this execution.
